A video of one of Apple's most iconic Q&A sessions from the past 20 years has recently surfaced online—watch it before Apple takes it down. See the video below.

Watch it before Apple removes the video

Even if you weren't closely following Apple in 2010, you've likely heard of "Antennagate" and seen Steve Jobs abruptly called back from his family vacation in Hawaii for that press conference.

If this is your first time hearing about it, here's what happened: shortly after Apple launched the iPhone 4, users discovered that the cellular signal would drop dramatically depending on how you held the phone.

The issue escalated quickly, and Apple held an emergency event just a few weeks after the iPhone 4 went on sale.

At the event, Jobs explained that signal attenuation was not unique to the iPhone 4, and gave users two options: a free case to prevent direct skin contact with the antenna, or a full refund.

After the event, Jobs, along with then-COO Tim Cook and Apple's Senior VP of Mac Hardware Engineering Bob Mansfield, held a Q&A session with the press.

Since then, there have been many different accounts of what was said at that Q&A session, including a recollection by John Gruber that he asked a question that prompted Jobs, Cook, and Mansfield to pull caseless iPhones out of their pockets on the spot, producing one of the most memorable photos of that era. However, the original video of the Q&A had never been publicly released. Until now.

Earlier this week, a YouTube channel called Sir Mix-A-Lot Rare Music (which doesn't appear to be affiliated with the real Sir Mix-A-Lot) uploaded the full 47-minute Q&A session, which you can watch below:

It remains unknown how the video was obtained, or whether Apple will issue a copyright takedown request. But since the video has already leaked, even if the original upload is deleted, copies will easily reappear elsewhere.

The fact that the video hasn't been taken down yet is a good sign. Still, if you want to witness this piece of Apple history firsthand, we'd recommend watching it soon.

Were you following Apple's "Antennagate" saga back then? Feel free to share in the comments.
